rv.q: This is as close to perfect theatre as you can get.

It’s typical of a few segments where characters are required by the script to express opinions which feel unnecessary and forced, simply as a means of tidying historical loose ends and generating theatrical friction.
However, in its attempts to make not wanting to get married into a kind of tragic flaw, Daniel’s Husband has wound up contradicting and simplifying its own messages.
Despite those final steps in the right direction, Daniel’s Husband‘s real potential remains in the shadows for the most part.

cn.t: McKeever's domestic drama about marriage and family rifts receives a mixed reception, with critics finding the living-room setting familiar but the exploration of unconditional love and toxic family dynamics resonant and harrowing.
